subject: Performance acceptance & close plan: MedCore MAP - hosted vs dedicated vs private
thread_body:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@medsys.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@medcore-health.com>, Procurement <procurement@medcore-health.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - performance acceptance criteria

Thanks Monica — quick note from our side before the MAP call. Our infra team needs an explicit acceptance checklist for performance across three deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private). Primary concerns: tail latency at 99th percentile, throughput at target concurrency (up to 800 concurrent sessions), and TTFT for cold starts (we care about initial response time for first token). Also want reproducible test harness and a plan for autoscale validation (how Redwood will verify predictable behavior during spikes). Can you confirm you can capture these items in the MAP and provide timelines tied to our close window (we're targeting PO by 7/22)?

Oliver
Senior Architect, MedCore Health

---

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@medsys.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - performance acceptance criteria

Oliver — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we expected. I'm attaching a draft MAP and a small benchmark extract so you can see our measurement approach. Summary of what we'll include:

- Acceptance criteria (explicit):
  - 99p latency (text-generation, 512-token prompts): Hosted: <= 420 ms; Dedicated: <= 220 ms; Private (on-prem): customer-dependent, target <= 250 ms with tuned instance.
  - Throughput: steady-state tokens/sec for 100k request/day workload; target concurrency saturation tests at 200/400/800 connections.
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token): cold start baseline + warmed KV cache baseline.
  - Jitter/isolation: percentile spread under noisy neighbour patterns.
- Test harness: JMeter + custom inference driver (we'll share containers + test scripts).
- Environment matrix: Hosted (Redwood shared clusters), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), Private (VPC or on-prem pack).
- Autoscale validation: scripted spike tests and controlled injection for canary windows.
- Rollout & canary schedule: canary on Dedicated 7/15 - 7/17, Private verification sandbox 7/18, final acceptance gating 7/20.
- Deliverables: bench-report CSV, TTFT graphs, and signed acceptance form (DocuSign link included).

I propose we treat the MAP as mutually owned: MedCore validates functional prompts and Redwood runs the perf suite in the three hosting modes. Rishi, can you confirm whether the Dedicated cluster we'd reserve for their pre-prod can be fully isolated for the 7/15 canary? Aditya, can you scope the tests needed for TTFT across cold-warm starts?

Attachments: MAP_MedCore_v1.2.xlsx; bench_results-hosted-dedicated-private.csv

Thanks — Monica
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - performance acceptance criteria

Monica — yes, we can reserve a Dedicated pool and ensure veth-level isolation for the canary window. Operational notes:

- Reserved cluster: 8xA100 equivalent instances, pinned to MedCore for 7/14 - 7/17. We'll disable tenant burst and routing fallbacks during test windows to get clean measurements.
- Autoscale: we'll configure the Dedicated autoscaler with deterministic step-scaling (no reactive burst) for the first run to observe predictability; follow-up runs will enable workload-based scaling to compare behavior.
- Monitoring: we'll stream token-level telemetry to a shared Grafana dashboard and export TTL traces.

I'll coordinate with infra to provision by EOD 7/12.

Rishi
Principal Sales Engineer

---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver@medsys.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - performance acceptance criteria

Oliver / team — quick technical clarifications on TTFT and the harness so our numbers are apples-to-apples:

- TTFT definition: we measure from request accepted at edge LB to first token emitted by the model runtime. For cold start baseline, we'll spin a clean instance and run 5 warm-up invocations, then perform 20 cold-start trials (fresh instance boot each trial). For warm baseline, we will sequentially issue 100 short prompts to simulate production cache utilization.
- Concurrency model: our driver will simulate session affinity where a session holds KV cache; concurrency levels 200/400/800 will be sustained for 10 minutes per window.
- Isolation tests: to simulate noisy neighbour, we'll run a mixed workload on the same host (30% heavy attention cases). We'll record p50/p90/p99 and also token-level CPU/GPU utilization.
- Private deployment note: on-prem results depend on customer infra (network hop counts and available GPUs). We'll provide a quantization/instance recommendation to meet target latencies.

I'll push the test containers to the shared Drive and include runbooks. Plan to land the first CSV (hosted baseline) by 7/13, full matrix by 7/18.

-Aditya
Senior Applied Engineer

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@medcore-health.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - performance acceptance criteria

Thanks for the detailed plan. A couple of procurement/questions before we lock dates:
- Can you confirm whether the Dedicated pool cost for the reserved window will be covered in a pilot credit (we discussed a trial credit in the last call)?
- For Private: if we need an on-prem appliance, what's the earliest delivery and whom do we engage for network validation?

If we can get those answered quickly, procurement can sign off on the canary window. Our target remains PO by 7/22.

Priya Sharma
Head of Platform Engineering, MedCore Health

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@medcore-health.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver@medsys.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - performance acceptance criteria

Priya — quick answers and next steps so procurement can move: 

- Dedicated cost: Marissa will confirm the pilot credit amount, but we will cover the reserved Dedicated pool for the 7/14-7/17 canary window under a trial credit (Marissa, please attach the credit note and confirm limits).
- Private/on-prem appliance: earliest readiness for an on-prem image + runbook is 7/20; network validation requires our infra partner (cc'd in the Drive runbook). We recommend starting with the Dedicated canary to validate workload patterns, then do Private verification in your staging datacenter 7/18-7/19.
- Docs & signatures: I've pushed the updated MAP (v1.2) and bench CSV to the shared Drive and kicked a DocuSign for the MAP acceptance gates. Links in the related_links field.

Action items & timeline: 
- 7/12: Redwood provisions Dedicated reserved pool (Rishi).
- 7/13: Hosted baseline CSV delivered (Aditya).
- 7/14-7/17: Dedicated canary (Monitored run; Rishi + Aditya).
- 7/18-7/19: Private sandbox verification (if MedCore provisions staging infra).
- 7/20: Review of full bench report + sign-off meeting.
- 7/22: Target PO/Close.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the 7/20 sign-off meeting and attach the pilot credit terms once Marissa confirms.

Thanks everyone — feel free to flag any risk to the timeline.

Monica
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
